text:
mia: Quick PSA: customers hitting flaky 429 handling in py-sdk. Some responses include Retry-After, some only have variants like `x-ratelimit-reset-ms` or `quota-remaining`. Current backoff util misses many cases.
omar: saw the same with a staging cluster yesterday. header names vary by proxy (case + suffix).
sam: minimal curl example I used:
HTTP/1.1 429 Too Many Requests
x-ratelimit-limit: 120
X-RateLimit-Remaining: 0
x-ratelimit-reset-ms: 1670000000000
(no Retry-After)
cheng: SDK expects `Retry-After` or exact `X-RateLimit-Reset`. Need tolerant parser that accepts ms epoch, seconds delta, and different casings.
mia: proposal: add parse_rate_headers(headers) -> RateLimitInfo dataclass with fields: limit, remaining, reset_at (epoch seconds). Normalize all common variants and prefer epoch seconds.
eva: also add async helper: backoff_and_retry_async(fn, *, retries=3, backoff_factor=0.5). Behavior: on 429, inspect Retry-After, then RateLimitInfo.reset_at, then exponential fallback. Return final Response or raise after retries.
cheng: typing: provide .pyi stubs and explicit overloads so mypy sees async vs sync helpers. Use dataclass typing for RateLimitInfo.
omar: tests: header casing, `-ms` vs seconds, missing headers using Date fallback, and no Date. Add small examples/ratelimit/aiohttp demo.
ci-bot: created GH issue #4123: "py-sdk: robust rate header parsing + async backoff helper" (https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk/issues/4123)
mia: I'll draft a short design note and start the PR. cc @cheng for types review when it's ready.
sam: I can write unit tests and the aiohttp example.
eva: thanks team :thumbsup:
cheng: will review typings on PR.
